name: Raumdeuter Counter 4-2-3-1

slots.why: Distributes quickly to the wingers or attacking midfielder to start the counter.
Defensive full-back stays back and lets the winger and raumdeuter do the attacking, which keeps the block compact.

Central defender. Cover is the alternate, as is the No-Nonsense Centre-Back (Defend or Cover), who clears rather than passes: the counter goes forward early and the pair is not asked to build. Only one centre-back may use Cover.

Cover centre-back sweeps up behind his partner. Defend is the alternate, as is the No-Nonsense Centre-Back (Defend or Cover), who clears rather than passes: the counter goes forward early and the pair is not asked to build. Only one centre-back may use Cover.
Defensive full-back on the right stays back for the same reason.
Holding midfielder screens the defence and does the simple defensive work.
Supporting midfielder wins the ball and starts the counter with a simple pass.
Raumdeuter drifts inside from his flank into the gaps between defenders and arrives at the far post; he does little defensive work.
Attacking midfielder plays between the lines and runs beyond the striker on the counter.
Winger (Support) provides the width the raumdeuter does not, so the counter is not all down one side.
Complete forward runs in behind or holds the ball up, according to what the counter needs.

description: A cautious 4-2-3-1 that defends in a compact shape and counters through a raumdeuter who finds space on the flank, an attacking midfielder and a quick striker.
whyGood: The raumdeuter's movement is hard to mark, so the counter arrives at the far post from a player the defence has lost track of.
whyThisShape: Defensive full-backs and a double pivot keep the team compact, and the front four are set up to hit quickly. The raumdeuter does not build play: he waits for the ball to be won and then runs into whichever space opens. The other flank has a winger who supplies width so the counter does not all come down one side.
whenToUse: Against a stronger team that will leave space behind its full-backs, when you have a smart off-the-ball player who scores goals.
whenNotToUse: When you have to dominate the ball, since only two players create; or when the raumdeuter cannot finish.

instructionRationale.Slightly More Direct Passing: Reach the forward outlets earlier without turning every possession into a long ball.
instructionRationale.Pass Into Space: Lead the mobile forwards and midfield runners into space rather than requiring every pass to arrive at their feet.
instructionRationale.Counter: Use the forward runners immediately after a regain, before the opponent can recover its shape.
instructionRationale.Regroup: Recover the defensive shape after losing possession; this is a positioning choice, not a measured guarantee about stamina or defensive success.
instructionRationale.Lower Line of Engagement: Let the opposition advance before engaging, keeping space for the forward outlets after a regain.
instructionRationale.Standard Defensive Line: Keep the back line at its mentality-relative default rather than explicitly pushing it up or dropping it.
instructionRationale.Distribute Quickly: Release the forward outlets before the opponent recovers.
instructionRationale.Distribute To Flanks: The selected outlets match where this tactic starts its build-up or releases pressure.
instructionRationale.Fairly Wide: Give the wide outlets space to receive and stretch the opponent without isolating every central passer.
instructionRationale.Low Crosses: A starting delivery choice for the receiving roles, to review against the actual forwards.
instructionRationale.Never Time Wasting: The kick-off baseline; review deliberately when score and time justify a different policy.
instructionRationale.Take Long Kicks: Use the selected forward or wide outlets without demanding short build-up under pressure.

keyRequirements: A raumdeuter with good movement and finishing
setupNotes: All three phases have been reviewed. Standard sliders are relative to the chosen mentality; unselected toggles intentionally leave FM to choose the response.
Player instructions use the selected role and duty defaults unless additional instructions are listed. Crossing and overlap settings are starting choices to review against the selected players.
